passages.text: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her abominations and tell her that this is what the Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites. Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me again.
He said these words to me.
He called me “son of man.”
He told me to speak to Jerusalem.
He told me to show Jerusalem her abominations.
The Lord GOD said this to Jerusalem.
He said, “Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites.”
He said, “Your father was an Amorite.”
He said, “Your mother was a Hittite.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ בֶּן־ אָדָ֕ם הוֹדַ֥ע אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֶת־ תּוֹעֲבֹתֶֽיהָ׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ כֹּה־ אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מְכֹרֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ וּמֹ֣לְדֹתַ֔יִךְ מֵאֶ֖רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י אָבִ֥יךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י וְאִמֵּ֥ךְ חִתִּֽית׃

passages.text: On the day of your birth your cord was not cut, nor were you washed with water for cleansing. You were not rubbed with salt or wrapped in cloths.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel about Jerusalem.
God described Jerusalem as a newborn child.
On the day you were born, no one cut your umbilical cord.
No one washed you with water to make you clean.
No one rubbed you with salt.
No one wrapped you in cloths.
passages.original: וּמוֹלְדוֹתַ֗יִךְ בְּי֨וֹם הוּלֶּ֤דֶת אֹתָךְ֙ לֹֽא־ כָרַּ֣ת שָׁרֵּ֔ךְ וּבְמַ֥יִם לֹֽא־ רֻחַ֖צְתְּ לְמִשְׁעִ֑י וְהָמְלֵ֙חַ֙ לֹ֣א הֻמְלַ֔חַתְּ וְהָחְתֵּ֖ל לֹ֥א חֻתָּֽלְתְּ׃

passages.text: No one cared enough for you to do even one of these things out of compassion for you. Instead, you were thrown out into the open field, because you were despised on the day of your birth.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the prophet Ezekiel about Jerusalem.
God described Jerusalem as a newborn child.
No one looked at you with pity.
No one showed you compassion.
No one did even one kind thing for you.
No one cared for you at all.
People threw you out into the open field.
They did this because they despised you.
They rejected you on the day you were born.
passages.original: לֹא־ חָ֨סָה עָלַ֜יִךְ עַ֗יִן לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָ֛ךְ אַחַ֥ת מֵאֵ֖לֶּה לְחֻמְלָ֣ה עָלָ֑יִךְ וַֽתֻּשְׁלְכִ֞י אֶל־ פְּנֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ בְּגֹ֣עַל נַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ בְּי֖וֹם הֻלֶּ֥דֶת אֹתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Then I passed by and saw you wallowing in your blood, and as you lay there in your blood I said to you, ‘Live!’ There I said to you, ‘Live!’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jerusalem through the prophet Ezekiel.
God described Jerusalem as a newborn child.
No one cared for this child at birth.
No one washed or clothed her.
She was left alone and helpless.
God said, "I passed by you."
God saw Jerusalem struggling in her blood.
She was weak and near death.
God said to her, "Live!"
God repeated, "Live!"
God gave life to Jerusalem when no one else cared.
passages.original: וָאֶעֱבֹ֤ר עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ וָֽאֶרְאֵ֔ךְ מִתְבּוֹסֶ֖סֶת בְּדָמָ֑יִךְ וָאֹ֤מַר לָךְ֙ בְּדָמַ֣יִךְ חֲיִ֔י וָאֹ֥מַר לָ֖ךְ בְּדָמַ֥יִךְ חֲיִֽי׃

passages.text: I made you thrive like a plant of the field. You grew up and matured and became very beautiful. Your breasts were formed and your hair grew, but you were naked and bare.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jerusalem.
God cared for Jerusalem when no one else did.
God made Jerusalem thrive like a plant in the field.
Jerusalem grew up.
Jerusalem became strong.
Jerusalem became mature.
Jerusalem became beautiful.
Her breasts formed.
Her hair grew.
But she was still naked and bare.
passages.original: רְבָבָ֗ה כְּצֶ֤מַח הַשָּׂדֶה֙ נְתַתִּ֔יךְ וַתִּרְבִּי֙ וַֽתִּגְדְּלִ֔י וַתָּבֹ֖אִי בַּעֲדִ֣י עֲדָיִ֑ים שָׁדַ֤יִם נָכֹ֙נוּ֙ וּשְׂעָרֵ֣ךְ צִמֵּ֔חַ וְאַ֖תְּ עֵרֹ֥ם וְעֶרְיָֽה׃

passages.text: Then I passed by and saw you, and you were indeed old enough for love. So I spread My cloak over you and covered your nakedness. I pledged Myself to you, entered into a covenant with you, and you became Mine, declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks in this passage.
He describes Himself as the one who passed by you.
He saw you.
You had reached the age for love.
He spread His cloak over you.
He covered your nakedness.
He made a solemn promise to you.
He entered into a covenant with you.
You became His.
passages.original: וָאֶעֱבֹ֨ר עָלַ֜יִךְ וָאֶרְאֵ֗ךְ וְהִנֵּ֤ה עִתֵּךְ֙ עֵ֣ת דֹּדִ֔ים וָאֶפְרֹ֤שׂ כְּנָפִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וָאֲכַסֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתֵ֑ךְ וָאֶשָּׁ֣בַֽע לָ֠ךְ וָאָב֨וֹא בִבְרִ֜ית אֹתָ֗ךְ נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה וַתִּ֥הְיִי לִֽי׃

passages.text: Then I bathed you with water, rinsed off your blood, and anointed you with oil.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to His people Israel.
God cared for Israel like a loving protector.
God washed Israel with water.
God removed blood from Israel.
God anointed Israel with oil.
passages.original: וָאֶרְחָצֵ֣ךְ בַּמַּ֔יִם וָאֶשְׁטֹ֥ף דָּמַ֖יִךְ מֵֽעָלָ֑יִךְ וָאֲסֻכֵ֖ךְ בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: I clothed you in embroidered cloth and gave you sandals of fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jerusalem.
God cared for Jerusalem.
God clothed Jerusalem in embroidered cloth.
God gave Jerusalem sandals made of fine leather.
God wrapped Jerusalem in fine linen.
God covered Jerusalem with silk.
passages.original: וָאַלְבִּישֵׁ֣ךְ רִקְמָ֔ה וָאֶנְעֲלֵ֖ךְ תָּ֑חַשׁ וָאֶחְבְּשֵׁ֣ךְ בַּשֵּׁ֔שׁ וַאֲכַסֵּ֖ךְ מֶֽשִׁי׃

passages.text: I adorned you with jewelry, and I put bracelets on your wrists and a chain around your neck.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jerusalem.
God cared for Jerusalem.
God adorned Jerusalem with jewelry.
God put bracelets on Jerusalem’s wrists.
God put a chain around Jerusalem’s neck.
passages.original: וָאֶעְדֵּ֖ךְ עֶ֑דִי וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה צְמִידִים֙ עַל־ יָדַ֔יִךְ וְרָבִ֖יד עַל־ גְּרוֹנֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: I put a ring in your nose, earrings on your ears, and a beautiful crown upon your head.
passages.sermon:
God is the speaker.
God addresses Jerusalem as a woman whom He cared for and adorned.
God put a ring in your nose.
God put earrings on your ears.
God placed a beautiful crown on your head.
passages.original: וָאֶתֵּ֥ן נֶ֙זֶם֙ עַל־ אַפֵּ֔ךְ וַעֲגִילִ֖ים עַל־ אָזְנָ֑יִךְ וַעֲטֶ֥רֶת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת בְּרֹאשֵֽׁךְ׃

passages.text: So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was made of fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You became very beautiful and rose to be queen.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jerusalem.
God gave Jerusalem gold and silver.
God clothed Jerusalem in fine linen.
God gave Jerusalem silk and embroidered garments.
God gave Jerusalem fine flour to eat.
God gave Jerusalem honey and oil to eat.
Jerusalem became very beautiful.
Jerusalem became a queen.
passages.original: וַתַּעְדִּ֞י זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֗סֶף וּמַלְבּוּשֵׁךְ֙ שֵׁשִׁי וָמֶ֙שִׁי֙ וְרִקְמָ֔ה סֹ֧לֶת וּדְבַ֛שׁ וָשֶׁ֖מֶן אָכָלְתִּי וַתִּ֙יפִי֙ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וַֽתִּצְלְחִ֖י לִמְלוּכָֽה׃

passages.text: Your fame spread among the nations on account of your beauty, for it was perfect in the splendor I bestowed on you, declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He gave you beauty.
He covered you with splendor.
Your beauty was perfect because of His splendor.
Your fame spread among the nations.
People in many lands heard about you because of your beauty.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨צֵא לָ֥ךְ שֵׁ֛ם בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם בְּיָפְיֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י׀ כָּלִ֣יל ה֗וּא בַּֽהֲדָרִי֙ אֲשֶׁר־ שַׂ֣מְתִּי עָלַ֔יִךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

passages.text: But because of your fame, you trusted in your beauty and played the harlot. You lavished your favors on everyone who passed by, and your beauty was theirs for the asking.
passages.sermon:
God gave you beauty and fame.
You trusted in your own beauty.
You relied on your reputation.
You acted like a prostitute.
You gave yourself to everyone who passed by.
You let anyone take your beauty.
passages.original: וַתִּבְטְחִ֣י בְיָפְיֵ֔ךְ וַתִּזְנִ֖י עַל־ שְׁמֵ֑ךְ וַתִּשְׁפְּכִ֧י אֶת־ תַּזְנוּתַ֛יִךְ עַל־ כָּל־ עוֹבֵ֖ר לוֹ־ יֶֽהִי׃

passages.text: You took some of your garments and made colorful high places for yourself, and on them you prostituted yourself. Such things should not have happened; never should they have occurred!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God gave Jerusalem beautiful garments.
Jerusalem took some of these garments.
Jerusalem made colorful high places for herself from these garments.
Jerusalem prostituted herself on these high places.
Such things should not have happened.
Such things must never occur.
passages.original: וַתִּקְחִ֣י מִבְּגָדַ֗יִךְ וַתַּֽעֲשִׂי־ לָךְ֙ בָּמ֣וֹת טְלֻא֔וֹת וַתִּזְנִ֖י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א בָא֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: You also took the fine jewelry of gold and silver I had given you, and you made male idols with which to prostitute yourself.
passages.sermon:
God gave you fine jewelry.
This jewelry was made of gold and silver.
You took this jewelry.
You made male idols for yourself.
You used these idols to prostitute yourself.
passages.original: וַתִּקְחִ֞י כְּלֵ֣י תִפְאַרְתֵּ֗ךְ מִזְּהָבִ֤י וּמִכַּסְפִּי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ וַתַּעֲשִׂי־ לָ֖ךְ צַלְמֵ֣י זָכָ֑ר וַתִּזְנִי־ בָֽם׃

passages.text: You took your embroidered garments to cover them, and you set My oil and incense before them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God gave Jerusalem beautiful, embroidered garments.
Jerusalem took these garments.
Jerusalem used the garments to cover idols.
God gave Jerusalem oil.
God gave Jerusalem incense.
Jerusalem placed God’s oil before the idols.
Jerusalem placed God’s incense before the idols.
passages.original: וַתִּקְחִ֛י אֶת־ בִּגְדֵ֥י רִקְמָתֵ֖ךְ וַתְּכַסִּ֑ים וְשַׁמְנִי֙ וּקְטָרְתִּ֔י נָתַתִּי לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And you set before them as a pleasing aroma the food I had given you—the fine flour, oil, and honey that I had fed you. That is what happened, declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
God gave you food.
God gave you fine flour.
God gave you oil.
God gave you honey.
God fed you with these gifts.
You took this food.
You placed it before idols.
You offered it as a pleasing aroma to them.
This happened.
The Lord GOD declares this.
passages.original: וְלַחְמִי֩ אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֨תִּי לָ֜ךְ סֹ֣לֶת וָשֶׁ֤מֶן וּדְבַשׁ֙ הֶֽאֱכַלְתִּ֔יךְ וּנְתַתִּ֧יהוּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֛ם לְרֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ וַיֶּ֑הִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

passages.text: You even took the sons and daughters you bore to Me and sacrificed them as food to idols. Was your prostitution not enough?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God says, “You took your sons and daughters.
You gave birth to these children for Me.
You took these children and sacrificed them to idols.
You offered them as food to false gods.
Your acts of prostitution were not enough.
You did even more evil by killing your own children.”
passages.original: וַתִּקְחִ֞י אֶת־ בָּנַ֤יִךְ וְאֶת־ בְּנוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלַ֣דְתְּ לִ֔י וַתִּזְבָּחִ֥ים לָהֶ֖ם לֶאֱכ֑וֹל הַמְעַ֖ט מִתַּזְנֻתֵךְ׃

passages.text: You slaughtered My children and delivered them up through the fire to idols.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God calls the people His children.
You killed My children.
You gave My children to idols.
You sent My children through the fire for idols.
passages.original: וַֽתִּשְׁחֲטִ֖י אֶת־ בָּנָ֑י וַֽתִּתְּנִ֔ים בְּהַעֲבִ֥יר אוֹתָ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And in all your abominations and acts of prostitution, you did not remember the days of your youth when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your own blood.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem committed many abominations.
Jerusalem acted with prostitution.
Jerusalem did not remember her youth.
In her youth, Jerusalem was naked and bare.
Jerusalem wallowed in her own blood in those days.
passages.original: וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־ תּוֹעֲבֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ וְתַזְנֻתַ֔יִךְ לֹ֥א זָכַרְתִּי אֶת־ יְמֵ֣י נְעוּרָ֑יִךְ בִּֽהְיוֹתֵךְ֙ עֵרֹ֣ם וְעֶרְיָ֔ה מִתְבּוֹסֶ֥סֶת בְּדָמֵ֖ךְ הָיִֽית׃

passages.text: Woe! Woe to you, declares the Lord GOD. And in addition to all your other wickedness, you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty shrine in every public square.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says, "Woe! Woe to you."
You have done much evil.
After all your wickedness, you acted again.
You built a mound for yourself.
You made a lofty shrine for yourself.
You placed these shrines in every public square.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י אַחֲרֵ֖י כָּל־ רָעָתֵ֑ךְ א֣וֹי א֣וֹי לָ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ וַתִּבְנִי־ לָ֖ךְ גֶּ֑ב וַתַּעֲשִׂי־ לָ֥ךְ רָמָ֖ה בְּכָל־ רְחֽוֹב׃

passages.text: At the head of every street you built your lofty shrines and degraded your beauty. With increasing promiscuity, you spread your legs to all who passed by.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem built a high shrine at the start of every street.
Jerusalem made her beauty worthless.
Jerusalem opened her legs to every passerby.
Jerusalem increased her acts of prostitution.
passages.original: אֶל־ כָּל־ רֹ֣אשׁ דֶּ֗רֶךְ בָּנִית֙ רָֽמָתֵ֔ךְ וַתְּתַֽעֲבִי֙ אֶת־ יָפְיֵ֔ךְ וַתְּפַשְּׂקִ֥י אֶת־ רַגְלַ֖יִךְ לְכָל־ עוֹבֵ֑ר וַתַּרְבִּ֖י אֶת־ תַּזְנֻתֵךְ׃

passages.text: You prostituted yourself with your lustful neighbors, the Egyptians, and increased your promiscuity to provoke Me to anger.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem acted with great wickedness.
You prostituted yourself with your neighbors.
Your neighbors were the Egyptians.
The Egyptians were full of lust.
You increased your promiscuity with them.
You did this to provoke Me to anger.
passages.original: וַתִּזְנִ֧י אֶל־ בְּנֵֽי־ מִצְרַ֛יִם שְׁכֵנַ֖יִךְ גִּדְלֵ֣י בָשָׂ֑ר וַתַּרְבִּ֥י אֶת־ תַּזְנֻתֵ֖ךְ לְהַכְעִיסֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Therefore I stretched out My hand against you and reduced your portion. I gave you over to the desire of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jerusalem.
God said, “I stretched out My hand against you.
I reduced your portion.
I gave you over to those who hate you.
These haters are the daughters of the Philistines.
The Philistine women felt ashamed because of your lewd conduct.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֨ה נָטִ֤יתִי יָדִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וָאֶגְרַ֖ע חֻקֵּ֑ךְ וָאֶתְּנֵ֞ךְ בְּנֶ֤פֶשׁ שֹׂנְאוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ בְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים הַנִּכְלָמ֖וֹת מִדַּרְכֵּ֥ךְ זִמָּֽה׃

passages.text: Then you prostituted yourself with the Assyrians, because you were not yet satisfied. Even after that, you were still not satisfied.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem acted like a prostitute.
Jerusalem turned to the Assyrians.
Jerusalem did this because she was not satisfied.
Jerusalem continued her prostitution.
Jerusalem was still not satisfied.
passages.original: וַתִּזְנִי֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר מִבִּלְתִּ֖י שָׂבְעָתֵ֑ךְ וַתִּזְנִ֕ים וְגַ֖ם לֹ֥א שָׂבָֽעַתְּ׃

passages.text: So you extended your promiscuity to Chaldea, the land of merchants—but even with this you were not satisfied!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem acted with great unfaithfulness.
Jerusalem increased her promiscuity.
She turned to Chaldea.
Chaldea is the land of merchants.
Even after this, Jerusalem was not satisfied.
passages.original: וַתַּרְבִּ֧י אֶת־ תַּזְנוּתֵ֛ךְ אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנַ֖עַן כַּשְׂדִּ֑ימָה וְגַם־ בְּזֹ֖את לֹ֥א שָׂבָֽעַתְּ׃

passages.text: How weak-willed is your heart, declares the Lord GOD, while you do all these things, the acts of a shameless prostitute!
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says this to Jerusalem.
Your heart is very weak.
You do all these things.
You act like a shameless prostitute.
passages.original: מָ֤ה אֲמֻלָה֙ לִבָּתֵ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה בַּעֲשׂוֹתֵךְ֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֵ֔לֶּה מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אִשָּֽׁה־ זוֹנָ֖ה שַׁלָּֽטֶת׃

passages.text: But when you built your mounds at the head of every street and made your lofty shrines in every public square, you were not even like a prostitute, because you scorned payment.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem built mounds at the head of every street.
Jerusalem made lofty shrines in every public square.
Jerusalem did not act like a prostitute.
A prostitute accepts payment.
Jerusalem scorned payment.
passages.original: בִּבְנוֹתַ֤יִךְ גַּבֵּךְ֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ כָּל־ דֶּ֔רֶךְ וְרָמָתֵ֥ךְ עָשִׂיתִי בְּכָל־ רְח֑וֹב וְלֹא־ הָיִיתי כַּזּוֹנָ֖ה לְקַלֵּ֥ס אֶתְנָֽן׃

passages.text: You adulterous wife! You receive strangers instead of your own husband!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem acts like an unfaithful wife.
You are an adulterous wife.
You take strangers.
You do this instead of being faithful to your husband.
passages.original: הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַמְּנָאָ֑פֶת תַּ֣חַת אִישָׁ֔הּ תִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־ זָרִֽים׃

passages.text: Men give gifts to all their prostitutes, but you gave gifts to all your lovers. You bribed them to come to you from everywhere for your illicit favors.
passages.sermon:
Men usually give gifts to prostitutes.
You did something different.
You gave gifts to all your lovers.
You bribed your lovers.
You wanted them to come to you from every direction.
You did this because of your acts of unfaithfulness.
passages.original: לְכָל־ זֹנ֖וֹת יִתְּנוּ־ נֵ֑דֶה וְאַ֨תְּ נָתַ֤תְּ אֶת־ נְדָנַ֙יִךְ֙ לְכָל־ מְאַֽהֲבַ֔יִךְ וַתִּשְׁחֳדִ֣י אוֹתָ֗ם לָב֥וֹא אֵלַ֛יִךְ מִסָּבִ֖יב בְּתַזְנוּתָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: So your prostitution is the opposite of that of other women: No one solicited your favors, and you paid a fee instead of receiving one; so you are the very opposite!
passages.sermon:
You are not like other women who are unfaithful.
You act in the opposite way.
Other women receive payment for their prostitution.
No one asked you for your favors.
You gave payment instead of receiving it.
You paid your lovers.
You did not receive payment from them.
You are completely the opposite.
passages.original: וַיְהִי־ בָ֨ךְ הֵ֤פֶךְ מִן־ הַנָּשִׁים֙ בְּתַזְנוּתַ֔יִךְ וְאַחֲרַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א זוּנָּ֑ה וּבְתִתֵּ֣ךְ אֶתְנָ֗ן וְאֶתְנַ֛ן לֹ֥א נִתַּן־ לָ֖ךְ וַתְּהִ֥י לְהֶֽפֶךְ׃

passages.text: Therefore, O prostitute, hear the word of the LORD!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem acted like a prostitute.
God calls Jerusalem to listen.
God says, "Hear the word of the LORD."
passages.original: לָכֵ֣ן זוֹנָ֔ה שִׁמְעִ֖י דְּבַר־ יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you poured out your wealth and exposed your nakedness in your promiscuity with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children which you gave to them, therefore I will surely gather all the lovers with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around and expose you before them, and they will see you completely naked.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks these words.
You poured out your wealth.
You exposed your nakedness.
You acted with promiscuity.
You did this with your lovers.
You did this with your detestable idols.
You gave them the blood of your children.
Because of these actions, I will act against you.
I will gather all your lovers.
I will gather everyone you loved.
I will gather everyone you hated.
I will bring them all against you from every side.
I will expose your nakedness to them.
They will see all your shame.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה יַ֣עַן הִשָּׁפֵ֤ךְ נְחֻשְׁתֵּךְ֙ וַתִּגָּלֶ֣ה עֶרְוָתֵ֔ךְ בְּתַזְנוּתַ֖יִךְ עַל־ מְאַהֲבָ֑יִךְ וְעַל֙ כָּל־ גִּלּוּלֵ֣י תוֹעֲבוֹתַ֔יִךְ וְכִדְמֵ֣י בָנַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תְּ לָהֶֽם׃ לָ֠כֵן הִנְנִ֨י מְקַבֵּ֤ץ אֶת־ כָּל־ מְאַהֲבַ֙יִךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָרַ֣בְתְּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהַ֔בְתְּ עַ֖ל כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׂנֵ֑את וְקִבַּצְתִּי֩ אֹתָ֨ם עָלַ֜יִךְ מִסָּבִ֗יב וְגִלֵּיתִ֤י עֶרְוָתֵךְ֙ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וְרָא֖וּ אֶת־ כָּל־ עֶרְוָתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: And I will sentence you to the punishment of women who commit adultery and those who shed blood; so I will bring upon you the wrath of your bloodshed and jealousy.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem acted like an unfaithful woman.
Jerusalem committed adultery.
Jerusalem shed innocent blood.
God will judge Jerusalem as He judges adulterous women.
God will judge Jerusalem as He judges women who kill.
God will give Jerusalem the punishment of wrath.
God will give Jerusalem the punishment of jealousy.
God will punish Jerusalem for her bloodshed.
passages.original: וּשְׁפַטְתִּיךְ֙ מִשְׁפְּטֵ֣י נֹאֲפ֔וֹת וְשֹׁפְכֹ֖ת דָּ֑ם וּנְתַתִּ֕יךְ דַּ֥ם חֵמָ֖ה וְקִנְאָֽה׃

passages.text: Then I will deliver you into the hands of your lovers, and they will level your mounds and tear down your lofty shrines. They will strip off your clothes, take your fine jewelry, and leave you naked and bare.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem acted with unfaithfulness and idolatry.
God will give Jerusalem into the hands of her lovers.
These lovers are the nations with whom Jerusalem sinned.
They will destroy Jerusalem’s mounds.
They will tear down her high places.
They will remove her clothes.
They will take her beautiful jewelry.
They will leave Jerusalem naked and exposed.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֨י אוֹתָ֜ךְ בְּיָדָ֗ם וְהָרְס֤וּ גַבֵּךְ֙ וְנִתְּצ֣וּ רָמֹתַ֔יִךְ וְהִפְשִׁ֤יטוּ אוֹתָךְ֙ בְּגָדַ֔יִךְ וְלָקְח֖וּ כְּלֵ֣י תִפְאַרְתֵּ֑ךְ וְהִנִּיח֖וּךְ עֵירֹ֥ם וְעֶרְיָֽה׃

passages.text: They will bring a mob against you, who will stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem has acted like an adulterous woman.
God will punish Jerusalem for her sins.
God will give Jerusalem into the hands of her enemies.
A crowd will come against Jerusalem.
The crowd will throw stones at Jerusalem.
The crowd will kill Jerusalem with their swords.
passages.original: וְהֶעֱל֤וּ עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ קָהָ֔ל וְרָגְמ֥וּ אוֹתָ֖ךְ בָּאָ֑בֶן וּבִתְּק֖וּךְ בְּחַרְבוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Then they will burn down your houses and execute judgment against you in the sight of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God says, "Your enemies will burn your houses with fire."
They will judge you in front of many women.
I will stop your prostitution.
You will never again give gifts to your lovers.
passages.original: וְשָׂרְפ֤וּ בָתַּ֙יִךְ֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעָשׂוּ־ בָ֣ךְ שְׁפָטִ֔ים לְעֵינֵ֖י נָשִׁ֣ים רַבּ֑וֹת וְהִשְׁבַּתִּיךְ֙ מִזּוֹנָ֔ה וְגַם־ אֶתְנַ֖ן לֹ֥א תִתְּנִי־ עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: So I will lay to rest My wrath against you, and My jealousy will turn away from you. Then I will be calm and no longer angry.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God is angry because of Jerusalem’s sins.
God says, “I will put an end to My wrath against you.”
God says, “My jealousy will leave you.”
God says, “I will become calm.”
God says, “I will not be angry anymore.”
passages.original: וַהֲנִחֹתִ֤י חֲמָתִי֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְסָ֥רָה קִנְאָתִ֖י מִמֵּ֑ךְ וְשָׁ֣קַטְתִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א אֶכְעַ֖ס עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but enraged Me with all these things, I will surely bring your deeds down upon your own head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not committed this lewdness on top of all your other abominations?
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
You did not remember your youth.
You made Me angry with all your actions.
I will bring your deeds down on your own head.
This is what the Lord GOD says.
You have done lewdness.
You added this lewdness to all your other abominations.
passages.original: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ זָכַרְתִּי אֶת־ יְמֵ֣י נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ וַתִּרְגְּזִי־ לִ֖י בְּכָל־ אֵ֑לֶּה וְגַם־ אֲנִ֨י הֵ֜א דַּרְכֵּ֣ךְ׀ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ נָתַ֗תִּי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְלֹ֤א עָשִׂיתִי אֶת־ הַזִּמָּ֔ה עַ֖ל כָּל־ תּוֹעֲבֹתָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Behold, all who speak in proverbs will quote this proverb about you: ‘Like mother, like daughter.’
passages.sermon: People use proverbs to describe others.\r\nThey will use a proverb about you.\r\nThey will say, "Like mother, like daughter."
passages.original: הִנֵּה֙ כָּל־ הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל עָלַ֥יִךְ יִמְשֹׁ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּאִמָּ֖ה בִּתָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: You are the daughter of your mother, who despised her husband and children. You are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
passages.sermon:
You are the daughter of your mother.
Your mother despised her husband.
Your mother despised her children.
You are the sister of your sisters.
Your sisters despised their husbands.
Your sisters despised their children.
Your mother was a Hittite.
Your father was an Amorite.
passages.original: בַּת־ אִמֵּ֣ךְ אַ֔תְּ גֹּעֶ֥לֶת אִישָׁ֖הּ וּבָנֶ֑יהָ וַאֲח֨וֹת אֲחוֹתֵ֜ךְ אַ֗תְּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר גָּֽעֲ֙לוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁיהֶ֣ן וּבְנֵיהֶ֔ן אִמְּכֶ֣ן חִתִּ֔ית וַאֲבִיכֶ֖ן אֱמֹרִֽי׃

passages.text: Your older sister was Samaria, who lived with her daughters to your north; and your younger sister was Sodom, who lived with her daughters to your south.
passages.sermon:
You had two sisters.
Your older sister was Samaria.
Samaria lived to the north of you.
Samaria lived there with her daughters.
Your younger sister was Sodom.
Sodom lived to the south of you.
Sodom lived there with her daughters.
passages.original: וַאֲחוֹתֵ֨ךְ הַגְּדוֹלָ֤ה שֹֽׁמְרוֹן֙ הִ֣יא וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת עַל־ שְׂמֹאולֵ֑ךְ וַאֲחוֹתֵ֞ךְ הַקְּטַנָּ֣ה מִמֵּ֗ךְ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֙בֶת֙ מִֽימִינֵ֔ךְ סְדֹ֖ם וּבְנוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: And you not only walked in their ways and practiced their abominations, but soon you were more depraved than they were.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem did not only follow the ways of Samaria and Sodom.
Jerusalem did not only do the same abominations as Samaria and Sodom.
Jerusalem quickly became even more corrupt than Samaria and Sodom.
Jerusalem became worse than them in all her ways.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א בְדַרְכֵיהֶן֙ הָלַ֔כְתְּ וּבְתוֹעֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֖ן עָשִׂיתִי כִּמְעַ֣ט קָ֔ט וַתַּשְׁחִ֥תִי מֵהֵ֖ן בְּכָל־ דְּרָכָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did as you and your daughters have done.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD is alive.
The Lord GOD makes a declaration.
Sodom is your sister.
Sodom has daughters.
Sodom and her daughters did not do what you have done.
You have daughters.
You and your daughters have done things Sodom and her daughters never did.
passages.original: חַי־ אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אִם־ עָֽשְׂתָה֙ סְדֹ֣ם אֲחוֹתֵ֔ךְ הִ֖יא וּבְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית אַ֖תְּ וּבְנוֹתָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Now this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: She and her daughters were arrogant, overfed, and complacent; they did not help the poor and needy.
passages.sermon:
Sodom was your sister.
Sodom sinned.
This was her sin.
She was proud.
She had plenty of food.
She lived in ease.
Her daughters also lived in ease.
Sodom did not help the poor.
Sodom did not help the needy.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ זֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה עֲוֺ֖ן סְדֹ֣ם אֲחוֹתֵ֑ךְ גָּא֨וֹן שִׂבְעַת־ לֶ֜חֶם וְשַׁלְוַ֣ת הַשְׁקֵ֗ט הָ֤יָה לָהּ֙ וְלִבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְיַד־ עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְי֖וֹן לֹ֥א הֶחֱזִֽיקָה׃

passages.text: Thus they were haughty and committed abominations before Me. Therefore I removed them, as you have seen.
passages.sermon:
Sodom and her daughters acted with pride.
They became arrogant.
They did evil things in My presence.
They committed abominations before Me.
I, the Lord God, saw their actions.
I removed them from their place.
You have seen what I did to them.
passages.original: וַֽתִּגְבְּהֶ֔ינָה וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֥ינָה תוֹעֵבָ֖ה לְפָנָ֑י וָאָסִ֥יר אֶתְהֶ֖ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִֽיתִי׃ס

passages.text: Furthermore, Samaria did not commit half the sins you did. You have multiplied your abominations beyond theirs, and all the abominations you have committed have made your sisters appear righteous.
passages.sermon:
Samaria was a city and a people.
Samaria did not commit as many sins as you did.
Samaria did not even commit half your sins.
You committed more abominations than Samaria.
You increased your abominations beyond theirs.
Your many abominations made your sisters look righteous.
Your actions made your sisters appear more righteous than you.
passages.original: וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י חַטֹּאתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א חָטָ֑אָה וַתַּרְבִּ֤י אֶת־ תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ מֵהֵ֔נָּה וַתְּצַדְּקִי֙ אֶת־ אֲחוֹתֵךְ בְּכָל־ תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂיתי׃

passages.text: So now you must bear your disgrace, since you have brought justification for your sisters. For they appear more righteous than you, because your sins were more vile than theirs. So you too must bear your shame and disgrace, since you have made your sisters appear righteous.
passages.sermon:
You must bear your disgrace.
You have brought justification for your sisters.
Your sisters appear more righteous than you.
Your sins were more vile than theirs.
You must bear your shame and disgrace.
You have made your sisters appear righteous.
passages.original: גַּם־ אַ֣תְּ׀ שְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֗ךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר פִּלַּלְתְּ֙ לַֽאֲחוֹתֵ֔ךְ בְּחַטֹּאתַ֛יִךְ אֲשֶׁר־ הִתְעַ֥בְתְּ מֵהֵ֖ן תִּצְדַּ֣קְנָה מִמֵּ֑ךְ וְגַם־ אַ֥תְּ בּ֙וֹשִׁי֙ וּשְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֔ךְ בְּצַדֶּקְתֵּ֖ךְ אַחְיוֹתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: But I will restore Sodom and her daughters from captivity, as well as Samaria and her daughters. And I will restore you along with them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God promises to act.
God will restore Sodom from captivity.
God will restore Sodom’s daughters from captivity.
God will restore Samaria from captivity.
God will restore Samaria’s daughters from captivity.
God will also restore Jerusalem from captivity.
God will restore Jerusalem’s daughters from captivity.
God will restore all of them together.
passages.original: וְשַׁבְתִּי֙ אֶת־ שְׁבִ֣יתְהֶ֔ן אֶת־ שְׁבִית סְדֹם֙ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת־ שְׁבִית שֹׁמְר֖וֹן וּבְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ וּשְׁבִית שְׁבִיתַ֖יִךְ בְּתוֹכָֽהְנָה׃

passages.text: So you will bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you did to comfort them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem sinned greatly.
Jerusalem tried to comfort her sisters, Sodom and Samaria.
Jerusalem must now carry her disgrace.
Jerusalem will feel shame.
Jerusalem will be ashamed of everything she did.
Jerusalem will be ashamed because she tried to comfort her sisters.
passages.original: לְמַ֙עַן֙ תִּשְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֔ךְ וְנִכְלַ֕מְתְּ מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑ית בְּנַחֲמֵ֖ךְ אֹתָֽן׃

passages.text: And your sisters, Sodom with her daughters and Samaria with her daughters, will return to their former state. You and your daughters will also return to your former state.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God calls Sodom and Samaria the sisters of Jerusalem.
Sodom and her daughters will return to their former state.
Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state.
You, Jerusalem, and your daughters will also return to your former state.
passages.original: וַאֲחוֹתַ֗יִךְ סְדֹ֤ם וּבְנוֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ תָּשֹׁ֣בְןָ לְקַדְמָתָ֔ן וְשֹֽׁמְרוֹן֙ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ תָּשֹׁ֖בְןָ לְקַדְמָתָ֑ן וְאַתְּ֙ וּבְנוֹתַ֔יִךְ תְּשֻׁבֶ֖ינָה לְקַדְמַתְכֶֽן׃

passages.text: Did you not treat your sister Sodom as an object of scorn in the day of your pride, before your wickedness was uncovered? Even so, you are now scorned by the daughters of Edom and all those around her, and by the daughters of the Philistines—all those around you who despise you.
passages.sermon:
You acted with pride.
You looked down on your sister Sodom.
You spoke of Sodom with scorn.
You did this before your wickedness was revealed.
Now your shame is exposed.
The daughters of Edom scorn you.
All the people around Edom scorn you.
The daughters of the Philistines also scorn you.
All those around you despise you.
passages.original: וְל֤וֹא הָֽיְתָה֙ סְדֹ֣ם אֲחוֹתֵ֔ךְ לִשְׁמוּעָ֖ה בְּפִ֑יךְ בְּי֖וֹם גְּאוֹנָֽיִךְ׃ בְּטֶרֶם֮ תִּגָּלֶ֣ה רָעָתֵךְ֒ כְּמ֗וֹ עֵ֚ת חֶרְפַּ֣ת בְּנוֹת־ אֲרָ֔ם וְכָל־ סְבִיבוֹתֶ֖יהָ בְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים הַשָּׁאט֥וֹת אוֹתָ֖ךְ מִסָּבִֽיב׃

passages.text: You will bear the consequences of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
You have committed lewd acts.
You have done abominations.
You will carry the consequences of these actions.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: אֶת־ זִמָּתֵ֥ךְ וְאֶת־ תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אַ֣תְּ נְשָׂאתִ֑ים נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will deal with you according to your deeds, since you have despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD addresses you.
You broke the covenant.
You despised the oath.
You acted with contempt for your promise.
You did these things.
I, the Lord GOD, will act toward you as you have acted.
I will deal with you according to your deeds.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְעָשִׂית אוֹתָ֖ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑ית אֲשֶׁר־ בָּזִ֥ית אָלָ֖ה לְהָפֵ֥ר בְּרִֽית׃

passages.text: But I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God made a covenant with Israel when Israel was young.
God will remember this covenant.
God will establish a covenant that lasts forever with Israel.
passages.original: וְזָכַרְתִּ֨י אֲנִ֧י אֶת־ בְּרִיתִ֛י אוֹתָ֖ךְ בִּימֵ֣י נְעוּרָ֑יִךְ וַהֲקִמוֹתִ֥י לָ֖ךְ בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your older and younger sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of My covenant with you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem.
God says Jerusalem broke His covenant.
God says Jerusalem despised His oath.
God says, “You will remember your ways.”
You will feel ashamed.
You will receive your older sisters.
You will receive your younger sisters.
I will give your sisters to you as daughters.
I do not give them to you because of My covenant with you.
passages.original: וְזָכַ֣רְתְּ אֶת־ דְּרָכַיִךְ֮ וְנִכְלַמְתְּ֒ בְּקַחְתֵּ֗ךְ אֶת־ אֲחוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ הַגְּדֹל֣וֹת מִמֵּ֔ךְ אֶל־ הַקְּטַנּ֖וֹת מִמֵּ֑ךְ וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶתְהֶ֥ן לָ֛ךְ לְבָנ֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א מִבְּרִיתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: So I will establish My covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD, so that when I make atonement for all you have done, you will remember and be ashamed and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, declares the Lord GOD.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to Israel.
I will establish My covenant with you.
You will know that I am the LORD.
I will make atonement for all you have done.
You will remember your actions.
You will feel ashamed.
You will not open your mouth again because of your disgrace.
I, the Lord GOD, declare this.
passages.original: וַהֲקִימוֹתִ֥י אֲנִ֛י אֶת־ בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ לְמַ֤עַן תִּזְכְּרִי֙ וָבֹ֔שְׁתְּ וְלֹ֨א יִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֥ךְ עוֹד֙ פִּתְח֣וֹן פֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י כְּלִמָּתֵ֑ךְ בְּכַפְּרִי־ לָךְ֙ לְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
